sup:70740.text:
Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We are delighted to present our competitive quote for your requirements. Our price is €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel of 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. This offer remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.text:
Dear customer,
Thank you very much for your message - it is always a pleasure to hear from you, and we are glad to help wherever we can.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.40 per unit, Zahlungsziel 60 days net, a contract term of 36 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.
Here is the background.
We checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.
AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. That remains.
LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. That remains.
PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. That remains.
We have verified the recent decrease in the alloy surcharge as well as your updated volume forecast, which allows us to adjust our pricing.
We are agreeable to your requested 36-month contract duration and 60-day payment terms.
However, a fixed price over three years is not feasible; we must implement an index clause (AS-14404), bringing our revised offer to €5.50 per unit.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C.
We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.
And while we are at it: our whole range is at your disposal, so if there is anything else on your list, just send it over - we are happy to quote.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

decisions.tactician: A thirty-six-month contract gives the supplier the planning security and binding volume it values, and the cash model does not count that, so it may accept a lower price than the model suggests. step_25 opens with real anchoring room and costs us €247k at that price. It sits less far below the supplier's estimated cost than E0 (€4.91) or step_10, which lowers the risk of offending a supplier that is already reviewing small accounts. That matters because we depend on it as the single source for 370011. A clause option would only give away protection; recent index declines argue against one. The arguments cited are the downward index moves and our rising forecast. The delivery-score argument is left out because it would read as a squeeze.

decisions.tactician: o13 keeps the terms it has already signalled it wants: a db 0 % clause, 36 months and 60 d payment. The clause and the commitment have value to it that the cash model does not count, so it may accept less than the 1.5 % shortfall the model shows. The midway rung (€5.32, C €260,111) beats accepting either standing sheet (€263–264k). E0 at €5.24 is below our last effective ask on these terms and near or under its estimated full cost, so the committee would likely reject it, and it could risk a walk-away from a supplier already reviewing small accounts. The no-clause options (o1–o6) reach a lower C on paper but go against its strongly stated need for a clause, so they are likely to stall. Citing the 81 % on-time record adds legitimate pressure without being aggressive.

That beats the standing sheet at €260,111 by about €1.1k, and code values it at +0.1 % to the supplier, so it should be acceptable. It keeps the 36-month commitment the supplier values but drops the index risk. o1 has the same C, but o2 keeps the longer contract the supplier prizes, so it is more likely to be accepted. o8 has a worse C because of the clause cost, and o12's C is poor. The order_history argument (€5.84) is weak against prices that are already lower, so we cite no claims.

why.tactician: o2 at €5.50 with no clause and pay 90 d would cost us €258,962, about €1,150 less than offer:70740-5 at €260,111. But the supplier has already ignored exactly those terms three times. Resending them gains nothing and spends messages with an account-reviewing supplier. o8 at €5.43 costs us €260,299, slightly worse than the standing sheet, and rungs below its level are unlikely to move a committee that has stalled. E0 or a hold would only repeat the deadlock. Accepting now locks in about 88% of the possible saving from C_open with no walk-away risk.
